For any caller and any recipient, calling withdrawAll(recipient) on the correct contract never transfers ETH out unless the caller is the owner (i.e., address(c).balance remains unchanged when a non-owner calls); the mutant that does transfer before checking owner can send funds to a recipient even when msg.sender != owner, violating this rule.

For every caller and recipient and any initial contract balance, a non-owner caller cannot cause the contract's balance to decrease (no outbound transfer) when calling withdrawAll(recipient); the mutant that transfers before checking owner can make the contract lose balance when a non-owner calls.

For any caller and any recipient and any initial balance, a non-owner caller cannot cause C to send ETH out (address(c).balance does not decrease); the mutant that does transfer before checking owner can make the contract lose balance when a non-owner calls.

For any recipient address and any initial contract balance, if a non-owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance remains unchanged (no transfer occurs); the mutant that does the transfer before the owner check can reduce the contract balance when a non-owner calls.

For every non-owner caller and for any recipient that REVERTS on receiving ETH (i.e. a reverting recipient contract), calling withdrawAll(recipient) on the correct contract will NOT cause the call to revert (the call returns normally and contract balance stays unchanged); the mutant which does the transfer before checking owner will attempt the transfer first, causing the call to revert when the recipient rejects funds, thus the mutant can revert while the reference never does for those inputs.
